column1: A settings change applies to every open work order, not just new ones
column5:
1. You are signed in with Settings > App Settings.
2. Several open work orders exist in various statuses with outstanding parts and unapproved lines.
column6:
1. Turn "Require ordering parts" off and check outstanding parts across open work orders.
2. Turn "Require picking inventory parts" off and check outstanding inventory/found parts.
3. Turn "Require receiving parts before completion" off, then on, and check whether invoicing is blocked.
4. Turn "Require approval for new lines" off and check Needs-Approval lines.
column7:
1. The change applies to every open work order whatever its status, not only to work created afterwards.
2. Require ordering off: outstanding parts are recorded as ordered and the Order action disappears.
3. Require picking off: outstanding inventory and found parts are marked as picked and the Pick action disappears.
4. Require receiving off: outstanding parts stop blocking invoicing and stay outstanding, Receive moves to the ... menu. On: outstanding parts start blocking invoicing, nothing is auto-received, so a WO that was invoiceable may no longer be.
5. Require approval off: every line in Needs Approval becomes Approved (turning an estimate into approved work). On: lines already approved stay approved.
6. Statuses change in the underlying records, not only in the interface; invoicing checks the same state.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9248 (Story 2, Settings apply to every work order) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 23, read on 21 August 2026.

column1: An approved line completes whatever the state of its parts
column5:
1. You are signed in with Work Orders: Create & Edit and WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View.
2. An approved line has parts that are unordered, unpicked and unreceived in various combinations, with each parts setting on.
column6:
1. On an approved line with an unordered part (ordering required), press Complete.
2. On an approved line with an unpicked inventory part (picking required), press Complete.
3. On an approved line with an ordered-but-unreceived part (receiving required), press Complete.
column7:
1. The line completes in every case; unordered, unpicked and unreceived parts do not prevent it, in any combination.
2. Ordering required, part never ordered: the line completes; the part stays waiting to be ordered.
3. Picking required, inventory part not picked: the line completes; invoicing still requires the pick, so the part is picked before the work order closes.
4. Receiving required, part ordered but not received: the line completes; the work order cannot be invoiced until that part is received or deferred with Received later.
5. Completing a line changes nothing about its parts — they keep whatever status the settings gave them.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9251 (Story 5, Parts no longer block completing a line) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 23, read on 21 August 2026.

column1: Bulk approve/decline judges each line and never sweeps a declined line
column5:
1. You are signed in with WO Lines: Create & Edit + Full View.
2. A selection mixes Needs Approval, Approved, Declined and Completed lines, one holding received parts.
column6:
1. Select the mixed set and run Approve.
2. Run Decline on a selection.
3. Run Authorization required on a selection.
column7:
1. Each selected line is judged on its own by the single-line rule; every qualifying line goes through and one failure does not stop the rest.
2. A declined line is never swept up: it is left alone by Approve and by Authorization required and is not in either count.
3. Approve counts lines in Needs Approval; Decline counts lines in Needs Approval and Approved; Authorization required counts lines in Approved; completed lines are excluded from all three.
4. Approving a declined line stays possible from the line itself (only the bulk path leaves declined lines out).
5. The result names each failure with its line number and reason in one message, for example "3 lines approved. 1 line couldn't be declined: Line 3, parts must be returned first".
6. Undo restores only the lines that changed, to the status they held.

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9254 (Story 8, Bulk approve and decline) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 23, read on 21 August 2026.

column1: Money follows See Financial Data; work follows View mode
column5:
1. You can sign in as a user with See Financial Data and one without, and in Tech View and Full View.
2. Receiving and invoicing surfaces are reachable.
column6:
1. As a user without See Financial Data, open a receive surface and check money fields.
2. Compare Tech View vs Full View for which actions/columns of work show.
column7:
1. See Financial Data governs money (cost, tax, subtotals, totals, sell price); View mode (Tech/Full) governs which actions and columns of work a user sees - they never compete on the same row.
2. No money field is ever both hidden and required: receiving needs a cost and a tax, both always prefilled, so a user without See Financial Data receives with those fields removed and the existing values standing.
3. Where a user cannot see money, those fields are removed rather than masked, and no text that reveals a price by implication is rendered (such as a cost-vs-sell warning).

---
This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8683 and story SV-9267 (Story 21, Permissions on the new surfaces) and the Simple Flow V2 specification version 23 and the permission map SV-8183, read on 21 August 2026.
